subject: Technical deep dive — latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-03T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Technical deep dive — latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology (Acme Health)

Thanks again for the call today, Samantha (and Evan) — good discussion. Below is a concise recap of the technical requirements we heard, our preliminary recommendations, and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

1) Primary pain points / goals we captured
- Latency spikes impacting UX: p95 spikes up to ~1.5s under current hosted setup (observed at ~512-token responses).
- Peak throughput needs during business hours: ~50–60 req/s; baseline average ~10–20 req/s.
- Data residency / PHI: traffic will contain protected health information and must stay within tenant VPC or dedicated environment.
- Predictable cost and ability to scale for campaign-driven burst windows.

2) Technical constraints you shared
- Average request size: ~180 tokens; peak 400–600 tokens in some workflows.
- Tight 99th percentile requirement for critical paths: target 99th <= 700ms if possible (you confirmed this is a soft threshold for non-chat, and a hard requirement for clinician-facing flows).
- Existing infra: long-term preference for VPC/private deployment; open to a short pilot on Redwood Dedicated to validate performance.

3) Preliminary sizing & options (high-level)
Option A — Redwood Dedicated (managed, single-tenant GPU pool)
- Model: Llama-2-70B-chat (4-bit quantized) or equivalent open-chat model.
- Hardware: 8x A100-80GB (or equivalent H100/NVLink) pool recommended for sustained 50–60 req/s at ~200 tokens, with dynamic batching (max batch 6–8) and KV cache warmers.
- Expected latency (estimate): p50 ~70–120ms per token; p95 for 180-token response ~220–350ms with batching off on tail-sensitive routes.
- Pros: fastest time-to-validate, billing transparency, Redwood handles autoscale and reliability.
- Cons: additional policy work for PHI; can be mitigated with dedicated networking and contractual controls.

Option B — Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem)
- Deployment: Customer VPC with Redwood control plane (private connectivity), option to run inference nodes on your cloud accounts or on-prem racks.
- Model & quant: same model choices; on-prem gives you full control of residency and keys (KMS/HSM).
- Expected latency: similar to Dedicated if equivalent GPUs are provisioned; networking plus placement in-region reduces RTT.
- Pros: meets PHI/residency needs, stronger audit controls.
- Cons: slightly longer lead time for provisioning and compliance sign-off.

Performance optimizations we'll apply in both cases
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and static context.
- Continuous batching tuned by route to balance tail latency vs cost.
- Quantization recommendations (4-bit + selective fp16 kernels on attention) to reduce memory footprint while preserving quality.
- Warm-up / cache priming during predictable bursts.

4) Proposed SLOs to validate in POC (two-tier)
- Clinical UI (critical): p95 latency <= 700ms, availability 99.9%
- Supplementary analytics/async flows: p95 <= 2000ms, availability 99%
- Throughput target during POC: sustained 40 req/s with 3x burst capacity to 70 req/s for short windows

5) Next steps (agreed actions)
- Redwood: provide a short PoC plan + baseline sizing by EOD Friday (I attached the architecture sketch & MAP).
- Acme: share sample prompt set, traffic shape (per-minute QPS), and a sanitized log sample or traces (no PHI) for sizing.
- Security: Acme to send SOC2 evidence checklist we can map to our controls; we will share our SOC2 summary + Data Processing Addendum.
- Schedule: 30-min follow-up on 2026-05-07 to lock POC scope and signing path.

Attachments: redwood_architecture_sketch.pdf (sketch, single page), mutual-action-plan-acme.xlsx

If I missed anything or you want the recap reshaped, tell me and I will revise. Otherwise I’ll follow up with the PoC sizing and a calendar invite for 5/7.

Thanks,

--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Technical deep dive — latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology (Acme Health)

Thanks Dylan — this summary is helpful and aligns with what Evan and I discussed. A few clarifications from our side:
- 99th vs 99th: for clinician-facing flows our hard requirement is 99th <= 700ms (not 95th). Non-clinical assistant flows can tolerate higher tail latency.
- Traffic shape: average 15 req/s, daily peak windows ~60 req/s (15–20 minute spikes tied to batch jobs).
- Token distributions: average 180 tokens; the 400–600 token edge cases are rare (~5% of requests).
- Security: we will need a mapped SOC2 report and confirmation that PHI can be isolated in a VPC/private deployment. Please include the DPA language in the MAP.

We’re leaning toward starting with Redwood Dedicated to iterate quickly, then migrating to Private/VPC once controls are validated.

Can you also confirm an initial budget band for the 2-week PoC (rough number is fine) — we’ll need to align purchasing.

Samantha
CTO, Acme Health
--
Samantha Cho

Subject: Re: Technical deep dive — latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology (Acme Health)

Appreciate the clarifications, Samantha — that helps. Quick answers: 
- We can design the PoC to validate 99th <= 700ms for the clinician workflow specifically by dedicating a tail-sensitive route (no batching) and pre-warming KV cache.
- Initial PoC budget band: $8k–$15k (two-week reserved capacity + engineering support), final number depends on exact GPU selection and logging/retention choices. We’ll provide a more detailed estimate in the sizing doc.
- SOC2 & DPA: sending the SOC2 summary and a DPA template as part of the MAP package (attached).

I’ll schedule the 30-min follow-up for 2026-05-07 10:00am PT and send calendar invites. Can you assign a technical contact who can share the sample prompts and a sanitized trace? Evan or someone on infra?

Thanks,

Dylan
